title: Reciprocal-tail cancellation metabolism and finite negative-mass rigidity

concepts.label: dynamic reduced-tail cancellation
concepts.note: Reduction by the changing tail gcd introduces a cancellation factor controlled by the overlap between the current multiplier and the reduced denominator.

concepts.label: strict gcd-growth budget
concepts.note: Every strict step of a positive divisibility chain consumes at least one binary factor, converting subexponential size into sublinear strict-growth count.

concepts.label: arbitrarily late constant-gcd blocks
concepts.note: A sublinear strict-growth count forces finite blocks of any prescribed length on which a positive divisibility chain is constant.

concepts.label: near-unit tail growth
concepts.note: Division-free normalised error vanishing bounds every sufficiently late tail step by an arbitrarily close rational factor (q+1)/q.

concepts.label: near-unit to subexponential bridge
concepts.note: Uniform eventual near-unit bounds imply that every fixed power of the tail is eventually dominated by 2^n.

concepts.label: normalised negative relative mass
concepts.note: The quantity (-E_n)_+/C_n measures precisely the multiplicative upward pressure exerted by negative centred-error excursions.

concepts.label: finite negative-mass endpoint
concepts.note: Summable negative relative mass bounds the integer tail; division-free normalised vanishing then forces the centred error and ultimately the Sylvester defect to vanish.

concepts.label: unbounded divergent-mass excursion frontier
concepts.note: After the paper's exclusions, the surviving state-system regime has unbounded negative excursions along a cofinal set and divergent normalised negative mass; the bridge from the original analytic problem remains open.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED EXACT BOUNDS: in one dynamically reduced exact-tail step between coprime state pairs, the old overlap d=gcd(a,v) divides the removed cancellation factor h and h divides d^2; moreover h=1 exactly when a and v are coprime.
statement_nodes.engine: coprimality cancellation applied to the two normalised step equations
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: No priority or novelty claim is made. The result is an exact arithmetic interface internal to the dynamically reduced state system.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The sandwich controls one cancellation factor but does not force it to be one, make the tail gcd globally stable, or rule out an infinite non-Sylvester orbit.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED BUDGET: if G is a positive divisibility chain, r strict increases before an endpoint force 2^r G(0)<=G(n), with the same bound after any shifted index; consequently, if every fixed power G(n)^K is eventually below 2^n, then the strict-growth count is sublinear in the division-free sense K r(n)<n.
statement_nodes.engine: each strict divisibility step at least doubles the chain value, followed by comparison of powers of two
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The doubling budget is elementary. The contribution recorded here is its exact natural-number interface for tail-gcd growth, not a claim of a new density theorem.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The conclusion is density-zero/sublinear growth, not eventual constancy. It requires a positive divisibility chain and the stated power-versus-2^n subexponential input.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED COMPACTNESS SUBSTITUTE: if the strict-growth count of a positive divisibility chain is sublinear, then beyond every lower bound and for every finite length L there is a block of length L on which the chain is exactly constant.
open_antecedents: sublinear strict-growth count for the chain under study
statement_nodes.engine: pigeonhole over aligned blocks, then divisibility monotonicity upgrades absence of strict steps to equality
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: No priority claim is made. This is an elementary finite-block consequence of sublinear event count.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Arbitrarily late constant blocks of each finite length do not imply one infinite constant tail or eventual gcd stabilisation.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED REPRESENTATION AND CLASSIFICATION: reducing consecutive exact tail states by their actual gcds gives a dynamic normalised cocycle whose factor is the quotient of successive gcds; that factor lies between gcd(a,v) and its square and equals one exactly when the current multiplier is coprime to the reduced denominator.
statement_nodes.engine: exact division by consecutive tail gcds followed by the abstract cancellation-factor sandwich
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: No priority or novelty claim is made for this exact reduction of the paper's integer state.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The result describes each actual cancellation event but supplies no global anti-shadowing theorem and no termination of changing-gcd behaviour.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED CONDITIONAL BRIDGE: the division-free bound K|E_n|<C_n gives the local inequality K C_(n+1)<(K+1)C_n; if such near-unit bounds eventually hold for every positive K, then every fixed power C_n^r is eventually below 2^n. Thus normalised centred-error vanishing implies subexponential tail growth for an exact orbit.
statement_nodes.engine: iterate denominator-cleared near-unit inequalities, select a rational rate whose fixed power is slower than doubling, and absorb the finite prefix geometrically
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: No priority claim is made. This is the formal analytic-accumulation bridge internal to the centred-state programme.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Normalised vanishing is assumed, not derived from rationality and a_(n+1)/a_n^2 tending to one. The theorem controls C but does not itself force E to vanish.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED CONDITIONAL CONSEQUENCE: along an exact positive natural tail, normalised centred-error vanishing makes strict growth of gcd(C_n,D_n) sublinear; therefore the actual tail gcd has arbitrarily late constant blocks of every prescribed finite length.
statement_nodes.engine: normalised vanishing gives subexponential tail size, which bounds the divisibility-chain event count and feeds the late constant-block theorem
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: No priority or novelty claim is made for the composed gcd-growth consequence.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Sparse gcd growth and arbitrarily long constant blocks do not imply eventual gcd constancy. They do not close the unbounded divergent-mass excursion regime.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED CONDITIONAL DISCRETENESS LEMMA: if a natural tail C is uniformly bounded by M and an integral error E vanishes relative to C in division-free form, then E_n=0 for all sufficiently large n.
open_antecedents: a uniform bound on the tail state
statement_nodes.engine: apply normalised vanishing at scale M+1 and use integrality to exclude every nonzero absolute error
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: This is an elementary bounded-integer consequence. No novelty claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The lemma does not supply the tail bound or normalised vanishing. Those are separate inputs in the finite negative-mass chain.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED EXACT ONE-STEP BOUND: for positive C and C_(n+1)=C_n-E_n, defining delta_n=(-E_n)_+/C_n gives C_(n+1)<=C_n(1+delta_n); positive errors contribute zero mass and negative errors account exactly for the possible upward step.
statement_nodes.engine: sign split on E_n and exact rewriting of the centred-state update
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: This is the standard one-step estimate behind a convergent-product argument. No priority claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: A pointwise growth bound does not imply that the product is bounded; summability of delta remains a separate hypothesis.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED CONDITIONAL PRODUCT LEMMA: if nonnegative relative-growth factors delta_n are summable and C_(n+1)<=C_n(1+delta_n), then C is eventually uniformly bounded; with division-free normalised error vanishing, the integral error E is eventually zero.
open_antecedents: summability of the supplied nonnegative relative-growth factors
statement_nodes.engine: bounded finite products of one-plus-a-summable-nonnegative-sequence followed by the bounded-tail discreteness lemma
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The convergent-product argument is standard. The node records its exact Lean consumer interface and makes no novelty claim.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The theorem does not establish summability for the centred state of an Erdős #243 orbit.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED CONDITIONAL ENDPOINT: if C_n>0, C_(n+1)=C_n-E_n, the errors vanish relative to C in division-free form, and the series sum (-E_n)_+/C_n converges, then the integral error E_n is zero eventually.
open_antecedents: summability of normalised negative mass from the original sequence hypotheses
division-free normalised vanishing from the original sequence hypotheses

statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The paper cites stronger results of Erdős–Straus and Duverney but formalises neither; it makes no priority claim for this conditional state-system endpoint.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Normalised vanishing and summability remain assumed. This theorem constrains the exact integer state system and does not prove Erdős #243.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED CONDITIONAL PAPER ENDPOINT: for an exact positive reciprocal-tail state, finite normalised negative mass together with division-free normalised centred-error vanishing forces a_(n+1)=a_n^2-a_n+1 eventually.
open_antecedents: the exact integer-tail model induced by the original reciprocal series
statement_nodes.engine: finite negative mass forces eventual centred-error zero, then the exact defect identity converts consecutive zeros into Sylvester steps
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The manuscript explicitly says this conditional theorem is weaker than cited results of Erdős–Straus and Duverney and recovers neither. No priority claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The state-system hypotheses are not derived from the growth and rationality assumptions of Erdős #243. The problem remains open; any surviving orbit must escape through divergent normalised negative mass or failure of an analytic bridge.

intra_zone_relations.basis: The actual quotient of successive tail gcds satisfies the abstract reduced-step equations, so the cancellation sandwich and equality criterion apply verbatim.
The dynamic reduction identifies what a gcd-growth event costs locally, while the strict-growth count bounds how many such events fit inside a subexponential global size budget.
The sublinear count produced by the exponential budget is exactly the hypothesis used to find arbitrarily late blocks without a strict step.
Normalised vanishing supplies the subexponential input needed for sparse gcd growth, but deriving normalised vanishing from Erdős #243 remains open.
Subexponential tail growth bounds the positive tail gcd and therefore makes its strict divisibility growth count sublinear.
The tail-gcd sublinear event count feeds the general constant-block theorem to produce actual late gcd plateaux.
The relative-mass estimate is the mechanism that will supply a uniform tail bound, while the discreteness lemma consumes that bound and normalised vanishing.
The generic product lemma accepts any nonnegative summable relative-growth factor satisfying the same one-step multiplicative inequality.
Convergence of the finite products supplies the bounded-tail premise; the bounded integral state then forces eventual zero.
The finite-negative-mass theorem instantiates the generic relative-growth factor with negativeRelativeMass.
The one-step negative-mass inequality verifies the growth hypothesis needed by the summable product theorem.
The paper-facing theorem first obtains eventual zero centred error from finite negative mass, then applies the already-authored defect-to-Sylvester recurrence theorem.
Both consume normalised vanishing: one uses summable negative mass to force complete rigidity, while the other obtains long cancellation-free windows without assuming mass summability.
The shared analytic input, normalised vanishing, is explicit in both theorem families and remains unproved from the original Erdős #243 hypotheses.
